subject: Banking
title: The Cost of Being a Bank
description: A fast breakdown of The Cost of Being a Bank for builders.

hook.text: Running a bank is expensive. JPMorgan spends $87 billion annually on salaries, technology, branches, and compliance.

buildup.text: Technology alone costs major banks $10-14 billion per year.

discovery.text: Compliance and regulation cost US banks $70 billion annually.

twist.text: Branch costs are declining. Each bank branch costs $2-4 million to operate annually, and customers visit less each year.

climax.text: Banks are technology and compliance companies that happen to take deposits.

punchline.text: $87 billion in annual costs. Banks are tech and compliance companies disguised.

quiz.question: How many technologists does JPMorgan employ?

details.summary: Running a bank involves enormous costs including regulatory compliance, technology infrastructure, branch networks, deposit insurance premiums, and capital reserves. These costs create high barriers to entry and explain why banking is dominated by large institutions.
details.whyItMatters: Understanding bank costs explains why fees exist, why banking is concentrated among large players, and why fintech companies try to provide bank-like services without holding a bank charter.
takeaways: Large banks spend over $270 billion annually on regulatory compliance globally
Technology investment is now the largest capital expense for most banks
FDIC deposit insurance premiums cost banks billions annually

faq.question: What are a bank's biggest cost categories?
faq.answer: Technology infrastructure is typically the largest expense, followed by employee compensation, regulatory compliance, branch operations, deposit insurance premiums, and loan loss provisions. Together, these consume roughly 60% of bank revenue.

faq.question: Why is it so expensive to be a regulated bank?
faq.answer: Banks must maintain dedicated compliance teams, file thousands of regulatory reports, undergo regular examinations, hold mandatory capital buffers, and pay into the FDIC insurance fund. These requirements protect the system but create enormous fixed costs.
